rationale: Agomelatine (MT1/MT2 agonist; t½ ~2h; no discontinuation syndrome; melatonergic sleep mechanism) to mirtazapine (NaSSA: α2-antagonist, 5-HT2/3 antagonist, H1 antagonist; heavy sedation; significant weight gain). Both drugs help sleep — agomelatine via melatonin agonism, mirtazapine via H1 blockade and 5-HT2C antagonism. Switching may increase sedation significantly. No serotonergic overlap hazard. Exit LFT check before stopping agomelatine. Start mirtazapine at 15 mg nocte and consolidate before stopping agomelatine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start mirtazapine 15 mg nocte. Continue agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Check exit LFTs. Counsel about increased sedation — mirtazapine sedation is more pronounced than agomelatine's. Take both at night. Warn about significant appetite increase and weight gain on mirtazapine.
Review mirtazapine tolerability (sedation, weight, mood). Continue agomelatine.

Stop agomelatine. Continue mirtazapine 15 mg nocte. No discontinuation syndrome from agomelatine. Titrate mirtazapine to 30 mg at 2 weeks if tolerated and response inadequate (counter-intuitively, 30 mg is less sedating than 15 mg due to additional noradrenergic activation).

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Agomelatine 25 mg → mirtazapine 15 mg (starting dose). Target mirtazapine 30–45 mg for full efficacy. Not pharmacologically equivalent — different mechanisms. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
